about: Hermann J. Wiemer, a vine grafter’s son from Bernkastel on the Mosel, planted some of the Finger Lakes’ first successful vinifera vines on Seneca Lake’s west shore in the 1970s and opened his winery near Dundee in 1979. Today his former apprentice Fred Merwarth and partner Oskar Bynke run the estate. They stopped using herbicides in 2003 and later moved to biodynamic farming, and in 2023 the home vineyard earned Demeter certification.

Flower Day shows that farming in the bottle. It comes entirely from blocks 1 and 4 of the estate’s HJW Vineyard and is picked early, on “fruit days” in the biodynamic calendar. In 2024 those were September 21 and October 5. The grapes are picked and sorted by hand, pressed as whole clusters and fermented with wild yeasts in stainless steel, with no additives, adjustments or fining. The winery counts it as its first Demeter-certified release, and it is vegan.

At 11% alcohol and under 1% residual sugar, this is the lightest and brightest of Wiemer’s dry Rieslings. The winery notes sweet citrus and summer fruit on the nose and a light, slightly spritzy palate. James Suckling found delicate Amalfi lemon and wildflower aromas in the 2024. The winery suggests it as an aperitif, or with a kale Caesar salad or grilled fiddleheads with feta.
facts: Two biodynamic fruit days, September 21 and October 5, 2024; hand picked
Whole-cluster pressed, wild-yeast fermented in stainless steel, unfined
